transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. Please do not attempt to regas your appliance yourself. Refrigerant systems are sealed and under pressure; attempting to open them without specialist tools is illegal in the UK, dangerous for you, and will permanently damage the system. Since both compartments are warm but the compressor is running, this usually points to an airflow issue rather than a lack of gas. To help narrow this down: Is the freezer compartment still cold to touch (even if not freezing), and do you hear any faint humming or buzzing noise from inside the back panel when the compressor runs? This helps distinguish between a simple blockage, a fan failure, or a defrost issue.
freezer isnt cold at all now, about 0C and everything has thawed. i can hear a fan going when the door is shut, and the compressor hums non stop. no clicking on and off

This suggests the cooling circuit has lost its ability to move air—likely because ice has built up inside and blocked the vents (often caused by a failed defrost heater or a blocked drain). To confirm this diagnosis, please unplug the fridge-freezer and leave both doors open for 24 hours to let all ice melt completely. Once dry, plug it back in. Does the freezer get cold again within a day or two?
24 hours is a pain, everything's already thawed anyway. is there a quicker way? the rating plate says R600a on it if that matters

There is no safe way to speed up defrosting; you cannot use hairdryers or heaters as that risks damaging plastic liners and causing electric shocks. The R600a gas suggests it uses a flammable refrigerant, so re-gassing is strictly for engineers with special certification. Your symptoms (compressor running constantly but no cooling) strongly suggest the evaporator coils inside are iced over because the automatic defrost system has failed—likely the heater or its thermostat. This blocks airflow, so even though the compressor works, cold air isn't reaching your food. To confirm this without waiting a day: unplug it now and remove all food into cool bags. Lay towels down, take out any shelves blocking the back wall of the freezer, and leave both doors open. Check if there is a solid block of ice or frost covering the metal panel at the very back of the freezer compartment. Is there heavy icing there, or does the panel look relatively clear?
theres no frost anywhere, the back wall of the freezer isnt even cold. thats with the doors shut and it all thawed already. what next?

Since the back wall is not cold and there is no ice despite the compressor running continuously, the appliance is not producing any cooling. This suggests a serious internal fault—most likely a failed compressor (internal valves have worn out) or a leak/blockage in the sealed refrigerant circuit. Please contact a repair service for this.
